title: The $\ell$-adic diagonal class over the completed coefficient sheaf
statement:
With the notation of [det-prop-diagonal-tower-system]:

1. $R\varprojlim_n\Delta_*\mathbf Z/\ell^n=\Delta_*\Zl$ and
   $R\varprojlim_n\mathbf Z/\ell^n(1)=\Zl(1)$, and more generally derived
   direct image along any morphism of the pro-étale sites considered commutes
   with $R\varprojlim$ and is computed levelwise on inverse systems.
2. The Tate twist $(1)$, defined as tensor product over the completed
   coefficient sheaf with the invertible sheaf $\Zl(1)$ (and $(-1)$ with its
   dual), is exact, preserves products and commutes with $R\varprojlim$.
3. $R\varprojlim c_\bullet$ is a morphism
   $\delta_{\Zl}:\Delta_*\Zl\to\Zl(1)[2]$ of derived $\ell$-complete objects; it
   is the derived $\ell$-completion of $\partial$, and it is in a unique way a
   morphism in $D(W_{\mathrm{proét}},\Zl)$ over the completed coefficient sheaf
   $\Zl$ of $W$. Its reductions modulo $\ell^n$ are the torsion cycle classes.

proof.text: For the reduction towers $(\mathbf Z/\ell^n)_n$ and $(\mu_{\ell^n})_n$, the transition maps are epimorphisms: the first are quotient maps and the second are the power maps identified in [det-prop-diagonal-tower-system](3), which are surjective by [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free](1), applicable because $\ell$ is invertible on $W$. The statement of [det-pe-milnor-epimorphic] says that an epimorphic tower has $R\varprojlim$ equal to its ordinary limit, so these limits are respectively the completed coefficient sheaf $\Zl$ and $\Zl(1)$ by the inverse-limit definition of the twist and the completed coefficient identification in [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit], with $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$.

The diagonal is a closed Cartier divisor: on an affine chart with local equation $t$ as in [det-prop-diagonal-tower-system](1), its open complement is $D(t)$. Distinguished affine opens are quasi-compact, so the complementary open immersion is quasi-compact. Apply [lem-exc-proetale-closed-exact] over $\mathbf Z/\ell^{n+1}$ to each quotient transition (regarding its target as a module over that same ring): the direct-image tower again has epimorphic transitions. Therefore [det-pe-milnor-epimorphic] also identifies its derived limit with its ordinary limit. The latter is $\Delta_*\Zl$, since direct image is precomposition on sections and sheaf inverse limits are computed sectionwise.

For an arbitrary morphism $g$ of the schemes considered, the induced morphism of pro-étale topoi, with the canonical identification of the inverse image of the constant sheaf $\underline{\mathbf Z_\ell}$ (or the canonical map on completed coefficient sheaves), is a morphism of ringed topoi [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. The inverse systems here are towers of $\underline{\mathbf Z_\ell}$-modules, not of modules over the completed coefficient sheaf, so we use the tower comparison stated for an arbitrary morphism of ringed topoi: [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison] gives the evaluation identifications $\operatorname{ev}_nRg_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}M_\bullet\cong Rg_*M_n$ and the canonical isomorphism $Rg_*R\lim M_\bullet\simeq R\lim(Rg_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}M_\bullet)$, with the total derived limit whose Roos triangle is that of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]; this is the asserted commutation and levelwise computation.

The item lives in the standing setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting] (a statement dependency of the item): $Y$ is separated of finite type over $k$, with $\operatorname{char}k\ne\ell$, and $\mathbf P^1_Y$ and $W=\mathbf P^1_Y\times_Y\mathbf P^1_Y$ are projective over $Y$, hence again separated of finite type over $k$; so $W$ is a scheme of that setting. The definition [sk-def-sp-tate-twist] makes $K(1)$ the derived tensor product with the locally free rank-one sheaf $\Zl(1)$ and defines $(-1)$ using its dual. More specifically, [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free](2) proves that the inverse limit $\Zl(1)$ is locally free of rank one over the completed coefficient sheaf, with the stated finite reductions. Apply the tensor clause of [det-formal-closed-support-ii-limits] with $X=Z=S=W$, both $i$ and $u$ the identity, and open complement empty, and $\Lambda=\mathbf Z_\ell$. Tensoring with this rank-one sheaf is exact because after the stated trivializing cover it is the identity on module sheaves; the cited tensor clause says it preserves products and fibers, and the natural map from tensoring $R\varprojlim$ to the $R\varprojlim$ of the tensors is an isomorphism. On a pro-etale trivializing cover, the dual of $\Zl(1)$ is identified with the dual of the free rank-one completed coefficient module, hence is again free of rank one; these local identifications descend to the dual sheaf. Apply the same tensor clause of [det-formal-closed-support-ii-limits] to this dual finite-locally-free module: its tensor functor preserves products and fibers and the natural map from tensoring $R\varprojlim$ to the $R\varprojlim$ of the tensors is an isomorphism. This gives exactness, product preservation, and $R\varprojlim$-commutation for $(-1)$ and proves clause (2).

Apply $R\varprojlim$ to $c_\bullet$. By [det-prop-diagonal-tower-system](2), $R\varprojlim\circ T$ is derived $\ell$-completion, while [det-prop-diagonal-tower-system](3) identifies the source and target systems; steps 1 and 2 therefore identifies the resulting morphism with $\Delta_*\Zl\to\Zl(1)[2]$ and shows that both objects are derived $\ell$-complete.

For the finite reductions use [lemma-weil-pbc-adic-completion-reduction] with the constant ring $\Lambda=\mathbf Z_\ell$, $I=(\ell)$, and $K$ equal to either $\Delta_*\mathbf Z\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathbf Z}\underline{\mathbf Z_\ell}$ or $\mathbf G_m[1]\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathbf Z}\underline{\mathbf Z_\ell}$. Tensor associativity identifies their strict reduction towers with the two towers of [det-prop-diagonal-tower-system]; each finite quotient is perfect, represented over $\mathbf Z_\ell$ by the two-term free resolution for multiplication by $\ell^n$. The cited reduction theorem identifies the finite reduction of the derived limit with its level-$n$ term; hence the reduction of $\delta_{\Zl}$ is $c_n$, which is the torsion diagonal class by clause (4) of [det-prop-diagonal-tower-system]. Naturality in $K$ identifies the reduction of the map itself, not merely its endpoints: the reduction comparison is adjoint to the tower projection, and the tower projections commute with $c_\bullet$.

To identify these reductions with reductions over the completed coefficient sheaf, apply [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] to $A=\mathbf Z_\ell$ and $I=(\ell)$ on $W_{\mathrm{proét}}$. Its canonical comparisons identify constant-coefficient finite reduction with completed-coefficient finite reduction, commute with the quotient transitions, and carry the completion unit to the constant-coefficient unit. Thus completeness of the displayed completed-coefficient endpoints follows from their constant-coefficient completeness, and the reduction calculation just made is the one in $D(W_{\mathrm{proét}},\Zl)$ required by clause (3). The map is initially linear over the constant sheaf $\underline{\mathbf Z_\ell}$. Since $W$ is a scheme of the standing setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting] (step 4), specializing clause (1) of [sk-lem-integral-models] to $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ identifies restriction of scalars from the completed coefficient sheaf with an equivalence on derived complete objects, so there is a unique $\Zl$-linear morphism $\delta_{\Zl}$. Full faithfulness gives uniqueness of the morphism with this underlying constant-coefficient map; no assertion that arbitrary morphisms are determined by their individual reductions is used.

The item is not the key statement of its unit, so no unit realized field is changed.

tool_uses.why: The item needs the generic fact that epimorphic coefficient towers have no R^1 inverse-limit term; the diagonal-tower unit does not provide this categorical limit theorem.

The item needs levelwise derived direct image and its Rlim comparison for towers of constant Z_l-modules along arbitrary morphisms; this generic ringed-topos statement covers that coefficient category, which the completed-coefficient tower node of the proper base change unit does not.
Fixes the total derived inverse limit of strict towers (with its Roos triangle) used by the ringed-topos tower comparison; generic, no diagonal-unit node gives it.
The item uses the general definition and local rank-one property of Tate twists to identify the tensor functor.
The item needs the generic finite-locally-free tensor preservation of products, fibers and derived inverse limits.
The item needs the constant/completed coefficient equivalence on derived complete objects to obtain unique completed-coefficient linearity.
The item needs finite reduction of a derived inverse-limit tower to its level term in order to identify reductions of the completed class.
Generic exactness of closed pro-etale direct image over a finite ring preserves each coefficient transition epimorphism; the diagonal unit does not supply this sheaf-theoretic fact.

Generic roots-of-unity transition surjectivity and local rank-one freeness over the completed coefficient sheaf, specialized to E=Q_l; this verifies the hypotheses of the Milnor and finite-locally-free tensor tools.

Its explicit finite-reduction and completion-unit comparisons identify reductions and completeness over constant and completed coefficients; the diagonal unit does not supply those generic scalar-restriction identities.
The generic integral coefficient identification, specialized to E=Q_l, identifies the inverse limit of finite constant quotients with the pulled-back completed coefficient sheaf on W.

In Stacks I checked tags 099L/099M/099I/0A07/093M against tags/tags, and read 0A07 (sites-cohomology l.5150) and 099I (algebraization l.1427). The statement is the verbatim blueprint text and was not changed. There are no new nodes and no SGA sources. Step 1: the towers are epimorphic (lem-pur (1), l invertible on W). det-pe-milnor-epimorphic with the constant Z_l ring gives lim = Rlim, and its cone convention agrees with the total derived Rlim because pro-étale products are derived products. The limits are the completed sheaf (integral-limit (3), E=Q_l) and Zl(1). Step 2: the complement of the diagonal is locally D(t), so it is quasi-compact. lem-exc-proetale-closed-exact over Z/l^(n+1) keeps the transitions epimorphic, and Delta_* commutes with lim. Step 3: the ringed-topos tower comparison (any morphism of ringed topoi, no ring identification needed) gives the levelwise and Rlim statements for constant Z_l towers. Step 4: Zl(1) and its dual are locally free of rank one, and the tensor clause of det-formal-closed-support-ii-limits with X=Z=S=W, identity immersions and empty complement gives products, fibers and Rlim. Steps 5-6: system (2)-(4) together with lemma-weil-pbc-adic-completion-reduction (Lambda=Z_l, I=(l), F_l torsion, Z/l^n perfect, K = Delta_*Z ⊗ Z_l and G_m[1] ⊗ Z_l) identify the reductions of the morphism itself with c_n, by naturality. Step 7: lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence compares the reductions and the completion units, and the equivalence on complete objects gives a unique Zl-linear lift. Repair (one E1-type unchecked hypothesis): steps 4 and 7 applied det-formal-closed-support-ii-limits and sk-lem-integral-models, which are stated only in the standing setting, without saying that W is in it. Steps 4 and 7 now state that W lies in the standing setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting] (already an item stmt_dep): Y is in that setting and P^1_Y and W are projective over Y. sk-def-sfb-dc-setting is added to their uses and proof_deps is recomputed. There is no cycle: a DFS over all dependencies does not reach the item.
